citations.location: VII. Analysis of the Enhanced Screening Protocol, Second opinion
citations.authority: 21 C.F.R. Part 117, Subpart B; USDA NOP standards
citations.cited_for: FDA regulations contemplate uniform application of preventive controls and quality standards across production; NOP similarly requires uniform quality and handling standards
citations.context: FDA regulations under 21 C.F.R. Part 117, Subpart B, contemplate the uniform application of preventive controls and quality standards to ensure consistent product safety and quality across all production. USDA NOP standards similarly require that certified organic products meet uniform quality and handling standards.

first_check.correct_citation: 21 C.F.R. Part 117, Subpart C (preventive controls); Subpart B covers CGMP only
first_check.explanation: Part 117, Subpart B is titled 'Current Good Manufacturing Practice' (sections 117.10-117.110). It covers personnel, plant, sanitation, equipment, processes and controls, and defect action levels. The phrase 'preventive control' does not appear anywhere in Subpart B; the preventive controls are in Subpart C ('Hazard Analysis and Risk-Based Preventive Controls'). Subpart B also says nothing about 'uniform' application or 'consistent' quality across production. Its general rule (117.80(a)) is only that all operations follow adequate sanitation principles and use appropriate quality control so that food is suitable for consumption. Nothing in it addresses applying different levels of screening to lots bound for different customers. The companion claim that the NOP (7 C.F.R. Part 205) requires 'uniform quality and handling standards' also has no textual basis: the only uses of 'uniform' in Part 205 refer to USDA's 'Uniform Rules of Practice' for appeals. The cited subpart supports at most a generic CGMP and quality-control obligation, not the uniformity claim the expert relies on.
first_check.evidence_excerpt: § 117.80 Processes and controls. (a) General. (1) All operations in the manufacturing, processing, packing, and holding of food ... must be conducted in accordance with adequate sanitation principles. (2) Appropriate quality control operations must be employed to ensure that food is suitable for human consumption

second_check.explanation: I could not refute the finding. I pulled the current eCFR text of 21 C.F.R. Part 117, Subpart B. Its heading is 'Subpart B--Current Good Manufacturing Practice', and it contains only §§ 117.10 (Personnel), 117.20, 117.35, 117.37, 117.40, 117.80 (Processes and controls), 117.93, 117.95 and 117.110 (Defect action levels). A search of the full subpart text turned up no instance of 'preventive control', 'uniform' or 'consistent'. Preventive controls sit in Subpart C, and the expert report's own materials list names Part 117's title, so it is the cite to Subpart B that is wrong. The closest support in Subpart B is generic quality-control language: § 117.80(a)(2) says 'Appropriate quality control operations must be employed to ensure that food is suitable for human consumption,' and § 117.110(a) says the holder of food 'must at all times utilize quality control operations that reduce natural or unavoidable defects to the lowest level currently feasible.' Read fairly, CGMP applies to all food a facility handles, so a weak inference against destination-based screening is possible. But the subpart says nothing about 'uniform application of preventive controls' or 'consistent product safety and quality across all production', so the report attributes content the subpart lacks. On the NOP half (7 C.F.R. Part 205), 'uniform' appears only in references to USDA's 'Uniform Rules of Practice, 7 CFR part 1, subpart H'. The nearest language is the definition of 'State organic program' activities, which ensure organic production and handling requirements 'are fully and consistently applied'. That is about government enforcement, not a requirement that products meet 'uniform quality and handling standards'. MISCHARACTERIZED stands: real regulations, cited for a uniformity rule (and, for Subpart B, preventive controls) that the text does not contain.
